turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what finally brought me in is... I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people and take pleasure in things has gone very quiet. Like my work—I'm a social worker, mostly handling substance abuse cases, and I used to really feel energized by it. Or my hobbies. I used to do a lot of yoga, and I loved going to art galleries. 

Actually, there was this one gallery downtown that had the most beautiful watercolor exhibit a few weeks ago. The artist was from Oregon, I think? Or Washington. Somewhere out West. I went to Oregon once for a graduate seminar, and it rained the entire time, which makes sense for watercolors when you think about it. The water just bleeds into the paper so naturally when the air is damp like that. I bought a really nice umbrella on that trip, one of those ones with the wooden handles... 

But, um... what was I saying? Right, the galleries. I just don't care to go to them anymore. Even my journaling, which I used to do every night. It's all just... quiet. I’m mostly just moving through my daily obligations at this point, just going through the motions.

Thanksgiving can be so draining. My sister insists on hosting every single year, but her oven is practically an antique. Last year the turkey took an extra three hours, and we were all just sitting around her living room eating celery sticks. 

Celery is such a strange vegetable when you think about it. It’s basically just crunchy water. Unless you put peanut butter on it, I guess. My clients at the clinic actually love when I bring in snacks—the peanut butter crackers are always the very first thing to disappear from the basket in the waiting room. I usually buy them in bulk at Costco. Have you been to the new one they opened on the west side? The parking lot is an absolute nightmare, they designed the lanes completely wrong so everyone gets bottlenecked near the tire center... but anyway, yeah, I don't think I've ever felt this quiet for this long before.

Which, honestly, has been a huge adjustment in itself. I found it at a flea market in upstate New York years ago. The guy selling it said it belonged to a local poet, but you know how those stories go—they probably just made it up to get an extra fifty bucks. Still, it had these little brass drawer pulls shaped like oak leaves. Oak trees are so fascinating, aren't they? The way their root systems communicate with each other underground... I watched a documentary about it on PBS one night when I couldn't sleep. The narrator had this incredibly soothing British accent. I think he's the same guy who does the voiceovers for those nature shows about the deep ocean. The ocean terrifies me, honestly. All that dark water, and those fish with the little glowing lights on their heads... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Eight months. Yeah, about eight months since she moved in.

He was telling me all about the laws of thermodynamics, how energy can't be created or destroyed, just transformed. It made me think about those old wind-up toys. It made this awful grinding noise on the linoleum. Our kitchen floor was that horrible mustard yellow color that was so popular in the seventies. My mom hated it, but my dad refused to rip it up because he said it hid dirt well. He was always so practical like that. He used to keep a spreadsheet for everything, even his lawn care schedule...

But no, I'm not feeling extra tired or anything. My energy levels are fine.

People are so quick to use words like 'failure' though, especially in my field. It always reminds me of those annual performance reviews we have to do every December. My supervisor, David—he's this guy who insists on using a red fountain pen for all the evaluation forms. Who even buys fountain pens anymore? He says it makes his signature look more authoritative, but the ink just bleeds right through the cheap paper they buy for the office. Once, he left it uncapped in his shirt pocket and it leaked everywhere. It was a crisp white button-down, too. He had to walk around the clinic the rest of the day with this massive red stain over his chest, looking like an extra in a slasher movie. I really can't stand horror movies, honestly. They rely way too much on cheap jump scares these days instead of actual psychological suspense. Hitchcock knew how to do it right. Rear Window is an absolute masterpiece. The way he uses the camera to make you feel like a voyeur, just watching the neighbors... 

But, um... what was the question? Oh, right, being a burden. No, I definitely don't feel like that.
